title: RNA Extraction, cDNA Synthesis and Quantitative PCR from NIH-3T3 Fibroblasts
author: Sreeja V Nair

steps.title: Plate cells in 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Seed 0.3 × 10⁶ NIH‑3T3 (or MEF) cells per well of a 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Lyse cells with Trizol
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL Trizol to each well, incubate 5 min at room temperature while scraping the monolayer with a 1 mL pipette tip to aid lysis.

steps.title: Transfer lysate and optional storage
steps.instruction: Transfer the Trizol lysate to a fresh 1.5 mL tube; lysate may be stored at –80 °C as a stop point.

steps.title: Add chloroform and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL chloroform to the lysate and vortex for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C to separate aqueous, interphase, and organic layers.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase and precipitate
steps.instruction: Using a P200 set to 50 µL, transfer the top aqueous layer to a new 1.5 mL tube, add an equal volume of isopropanol, and gently tap to mix.

steps.title: RNA precipitation incubation
steps.instruction: Either store the tube at –20 °C (optional) or incubate at room temperature for 5 min followed by centrifugation at 13,000 × g for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant with a 1 mL pipette and add 0.5 mL 80 % (v/v) ethanol to the tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 × g for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat step 8 (discard supernatant, add 0.5 mL 80 % ethanol) and repeat step 9 centrifugation.

steps.title: Remove ethanol and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant with a 1 mL pipette, decant any residual liquid onto a Kimwipe, and allow the RNA pellet to air‑dry.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA and assess quality
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 50 µL RNase‑free water, measure concentration and purity on a Nanodrop (260/280 ratio > 2 is ideal).

steps.title: Store RNA or proceed
steps.instruction: Store the RNA at –80 °C or continue directly to cDNA synthesis.

steps.title: Prepare 2X cDNA master mix
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare a 2X cDNA master mix according to the manufacturer’s instructions; for 4 samples include extra volume for 4.5 reactions.

steps.title: Add master mix to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Briefly spin the tube and add 10 µL of the master mix to each labeled PCR tube on ice.

steps.title: Add RNA and adjust volume
steps.instruction: Add RNA amounting to 500 ng (calculate volume from concentration) to each tube and bring the total volume to 20 µL with sterile water on ice.

steps.title: cDNA synthesis thermal program
steps.instruction: Tap tubes to mix, then run: 25 °C 10 min, 37 °C 120 min, 85 °C 5 min, hold at 4 °C; store at –20 °C or proceed to qPCR.

steps.title: Dilute cDNA 20‑fold
steps.instruction: Dilute the synthesized cDNA 20‑fold with sterile water.

steps.title: Prepare 2X qPCR master mix
steps.instruction: On ice, prepare a 2X qPCR master mix for each RNA; for four samples in quadruplicate (16 reactions) add extra for 2 more, total 18 reactions, requiring 180 µL mix (126 µL components before cDNA).

steps.title: Dispense master mix and cDNA
steps.instruction: Briefly spin the tubes, then dispense 7 µL of the qPCR master mix and 3 µL diluted cDNA into each well of a 384‑well plate as assigned.

steps.title: Seal plate and run qPCR
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, briefly centrifuge to collect liquids, and run on a ViiA 7 system: 95 °C 2 min activation, then 40 cycles of 95 °C 1 s and 60 °C 20 s; melt curve 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 1 min, 95 °C 15 s.
